rfi.title: Democrats sweeps Congress leaving defiant Trump a lame-duck president
rfi.description: US President Donald Trump was coming to terms on Wednesday with the prospect of two years of political impotence, after the Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in the midterm elections.

rfi.title: Trump says US will halt 'contentious' aid to Israel by end of year
rfi.description: United States President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday that Washington would end its annual $3.8 billion (€3.4 billion) in aid to Israel, based on a mutual decision. The news coincided with midterm elections in which support for Israel has been a contentious issue.

rfi.title: Democratic midterm wins threaten data centre boom in key US states
rfi.description: Strong wins for Democratic candidates threaten the prospects for energy-hungry data centres in key states in the United States, and could slow the AI rollout that has driven Wall Street over the past four years.

rfi.title: French judges open inquiry into allegation of Israeli war crime
rfi.description: French judges have opened a judicial investigation into a complaint of an alleged war crime, following an Israeli strike on a residential building in Beirut in November 2024, it emerged on Tuesday.

rfi.title: South Africa votes in local elections as growing anger threatens ANC
rfi.description: South Africans queued from early on Wednesday to vote in municipal elections, with anger over corruption, crime and failing public services threatening to inflict fresh losses on the African National Congress.

rfi.title: Corruption in Kenya taking massive toll on economic growth, warns World Bank
rfi.description: Corruption is costing Kenya billions of dollars each year in lost revenue, inflated business costs, and lost earnings for workers, while taking a huge toll on investment and economic growth, the World Bank said in a report published Wednesday.

rfi.title: PSG coach  Enrique hails 'sensational' Champions League win at Villarreal
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique on Wednesday hailed his team's performance as sensational after they blazed past Villarreal 6-0 to maintain their perfect start to the defence of their Champions League title.

rfi.title: Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike
rfi.description: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.

rfi.title: In Miami’s Little Haiti, ‘Blood’ looks past Trump’s rhetoric as US midterms loom
rfi.description: In Miami’s Little Haiti, a man struggling to find steady work sees opportunity in Donald Trump’s politics. The president’s false claims about Haitian immigrants have not shaken his support. For the man known as Blood, what matters just before the midterm elections is the promise of a chance to earn a living.

rfi.title: United Nations confirms end of Western Sahara peacekeeping mission
rfi.description: The United Nations has confirmed it has begun the process of ending its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, after Russia and the United States vetoed each other's draft resolutions on extending the 35-year-old deployment.

rfi.title: Nine out of 10 crimes against journalists go unpunished, Unesco says
rfi.description: Monday marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists – chosen in memory of Ghislaine Dupont and Claude Verlon, two journalists from Radio France Internationale who were murdered in Mali on 2 November, 2013. According to a report by Unesco, attacks and harassment targeting the press continue to go largely unpunished in Africa and across the globe.

rfi.title: French tennis star Fils starts bid for Paris Masters title and a spot in Turin
rfi.description: France's top tennis player Arthur Fils on Tuesday starts his bid for the Paris Masters title, and a place at the season-ending championships in Turin.

rfi.title: Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing
rfi.description: A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man.

rfi.title: Nigerian health chiefs confirm negative results in Ebola cases
rfi.description: Health authorities investigating two suspected Ebola cases in north-eastern Nigeria ​confirmed on Monday that both samples were negative after ‌two rounds of testing.

rfi.title: France braces for fresh protests as students to resume school blockades
rfi.description: France is readying for another week of protests after the head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart Monday, ahead of a nationwide day of strikes and protests on Thursday.

rfi.title: Miami voters weigh local hardship and America's global role as early voting ends
rfi.description: A massive thunderstorm and flash flood warnings failed to deter voters in Miami as they headed to polling stations on Florida’s final day of early voting ahead of the US midterm elections.

rfi.title: A year after the fall of El Fasher, Sudan's war has left a ghost town in its wake
rfi.description: A year after paramilitary forces at war with the Sudanese army captured the strategic city of El Fasher, survivors and aid workers report that the capital of North Darfur state remains largely abandoned. Some residents are too scared to return, while thousands are still missing – many held in deplorable conditions in overcrowded prisons.

rfi.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police
rfi.description: France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, midterms 2026 : dans son premier discours après une défaite historique, Trump parle de sa salle de bal à la Maison Blanche
lemonde.description: A la Maison Blanche, le président américain a réservé ses premières remarques à son projet de rénovation. Quelques heures avant, son vice-président a déclaré que « la véritable raison pour laquelle nous avons perdu est évidente pour presque tout le monde », à savoir la guerre lancée par son administration et Israël contre l’Iran.

lemonde.title: « Après les midterms, une obligation de renouvellement va s’imposer chez les démocrates comme chez les républicains »
lemonde.description: Les démocrates savent qu’ils ont moins gagné le 3 novembre que Donald Trump a perdu et que leur image est exécrable, décrypte Gilles Paris, éditorialiste au « Monde » dans sa chronique. Le Parti républicain va devoir, lui aussi, procéder à un droit d’inventaire.

lemonde.title: Budget 2026 : le gouvernement tente un ultime tour de vis pour éviter un dérapage XXL
lemonde.description: Le gouvernement a annoncé, mercredi 4 novembre, l’annulation de crédits pour 3,8 milliards d’euros. Mais il prévoit en parallèle 3,7 milliards d’euros de dépenses supplémentaires. Au total, le déficit risque d’atteindre voire dépasser 5,4 % du PIB en 2026. Le budget 2027 a, lui, été rejeté à l’unanimité dans la nuit à l’Assemblée.

lemonde.title: Manifestation du 5 novembre : Laurent Nuñez annonce 70 000 policiers et gendarmes déployés et prévient qu’aucun « débordement ne sera toléré »
lemonde.description: Les autorités prévoient « un peu plus de 220 actions de voie publique », dont la plupart ont été déclarées par l’intersyndicale, selon le ministre de l’intérieur.

lemonde.title: Procès de « l’inconnue de l’A10 » : la mère d’Inass Touloub s’effondre après la diffusion des photos de l’autopsie de sa fille
lemonde.description: L’audience a été suspendue mercredi suite au malaise d’Halima El Balkhti, survenu après l’éprouvant exposé de la médecin légiste. « Ce n’est pas un décès brutal, mais une lente agonie », a indiqué l’experte, en décrivant les multiples lésions, brûlures, morsures et fractures relevées sur l’enfant de 4 ans, abandonnée en 1987 en bordure de l’autoroute A10.

lemonde.title: L’Ukraine veut répliquer ailleurs la mission humanitaire menée à Olechky pour sauver des civils
lemonde.description: D’après la Maison Blanche, l’opération avait été négociée par Melania Trump. Volodymyr Zelensky lui a décerné, mercredi, une distinction honorifique.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Lens-Côme : les Sang et Or, humiliés, subissent la plus lourde défaite d’un club français en Ligue des champions
lemonde.description: Très loin du compte, les Lensois de Florian Thauvin ont subi une défaite historique mercredi, au stade Bollaert-Delelis, lors de la 4ᵉ journée de la Ligue des champions, compromettant largement leurs chances de se qualifier en barrages.

lemonde.title: Manifestations du 17 octobre : devant la commission d’enquête parlementaire, les commerçants disent avoir été « totalement abandonnés et sacrifiés »
lemonde.description: Entendus à l’Assemblée nationale, mercredi 4 novembre, plusieurs représentants d’associations de commerçants à Paris, Lyon ou Marseille, ont dénoncé la défaillance des pouvoirs publics face aux pillages lors de cette journée de mobilisation.

lemonde.title: Avec la cyberattaque au Crédit mutuel Arkéa, les banques européennes prennent conscience de l’ampleur de leur vulnérabilité
lemonde.description: Les pirates informatiques sont parvenus à dérober une partie des fonds propres d’Arkéa. Une attaque inédite dans la finance européenne.

lemonde.title: Pierre Coppey, ancien dirigeant de Vinci et militant associatif pour la réinsertion, devient Contrôleur général des lieux de privation de liberté
lemonde.description: Après avoir passé, mercredi 4 novembre, deux oraux devant la commission des lois de l’Assemblée nationale puis devant celle du Sénat, il succède à Dominique Simonnot.

lemonde.title: Agression dans une école à Nice : l’autrice mise en examen pour tentative de meurtre et écrouée
lemonde.description: Pendant sa garde à vue, la femme de 36 ans a contesté les violences, mais a reconnu avoir actionné plusieurs fois son arme – précisant qu’elle savait qu’elle était vide – et exprimé des regrets.

lemonde.title: Le Rwanda, ancien partenaire modèle des Etats-Unis, désormais dans le collimateur de l’administration Trump
lemonde.description: Washington a annoncé, lundi 2 novembre, l’exclusion de Kigali de l’accord commercial préférentiel AGOA, à compter du 1ᵉʳ janvier 2027. Une décision brusque liée à l’implication du régime rwandais dans la guerre en cours dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.

lemonde.title: Parcoursup : Sébastien Lecornu annonce une première réunion lundi pour réformer la plateforme d’orientation, sur fond de mobilisation lycéenne
lemonde.description: Lycéens et enseignants seront réunis autour des ministres concernés, afin de présenter de « premières recommandations courant novembre », a déclaré le premier ministre.

lemonde.title: Le Royaume-Uni devrait présenter des excuses officielles pour son rôle dans l’esclavage, mais refuse d’envisager le paiement de réparations
lemonde.description: Lors du sommet du Commonwealth qui s’est achevé mercredi, dans les Caraïbes, le gouvernement britannique a écarté tout débat sur les réparations liées à la traite des esclaves, que réclament les pays concernés. Le roi a lui exprimé son « horreur » face à l’esclavage.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi les juges d’instruction ont décidé de renvoyer devant la cour d’assises spéciale l’assassin de Dominique Bernard
lemonde.description: Par ordonnance en date du 4 novembre, les juges d’instruction antiterroristes ont mis en accusation Mohammed Mogouchkov, Russe de 23 ans, devant la cour d’assises spécialement composée pour être jugé pour son implication dans l’attentat, à Arras. Des faits qu’il a revendiqués tout au long de l’instruction.

lemonde.title: La grande nouvelliste Katherine Mansfield et sa prose fulgurante sont à redécouvrir à l’occasion de son entrée dans « La Pléiade »
lemonde.description: Une édition qui comprend toutes les nouvelles publiées de son vivant ainsi que de nombreux textes posthumes, études et premiers états. De quoi suivre au jour le jour le travail de l’écrivaine d’origine néo-zélandaise morte à 34 ans, en 1923.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Israël : Netanyahu assure qu'il existe de "graves soupçons" d'ingérence étrangère
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre Benjamin Netanyahu a affirmé mercredi qu'il existait "de graves soupçons" d’ingérence étrangère dans les élections législatives israéliennes. De son côté, la Liste unifiée, principal parti arabe israélien, a dénoncé une "persécution politique", après des accusations relayées par le camp de Benjamin Netanyahu affirmant que l'un de ses piliers, Ayman Odeh, était soupçonné de fraude aux législatives.

france24fr.title: Après la déroute des midterms, les règlements de compte commencent chez les républicains
france24fr.description: La guerre est déclarée, ou presque. Après la débâcle des républicains aux élections de mi-mandat, Donald Trump et ses alliés fustigent la piètre qualité des candidats, tandis que sur le terrain, les responsables locaux du parti pointent la responsabilité du président. Parmi les ténors, le vice-président J. D. Vance prend ses distances avec Trump en douceur et jette les bases d'une plateforme pour 2028, tandis que Ron DeSantis se présente à demi-mot comme une alternative.

france24fr.title: Midterms : une vague démocrate, et après ?
france24fr.description: C’est une vague bleue au Congrès américain. Un "bluenami", comme le décrit la presse américaine. Les démocrates ont pris le contrôle de la Chambre des représentants mais aussi du Sénat. Donald Trump a accepté le résultat des élections, tout en affirmant sur son réseau Truth Social que "les républicains auraient gagné si son propre nom avait été sur le bulletin". Quelles leçons tirer de ces midterms ? Est-ce un vote sanction contre Trump ? Est-ce un vote d’adhésion pour les démocrates ?

france24fr.title: Les attentes des Michiganais après l'élection d'Abdul el-Sayed au poste de sénateur
france24fr.description: Abdul el-Sayed, le candidat démocrate pour le siège de sénateur du Michigan, a été élu ce mardi lors des élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis, au terme d'une course très suivie. Qu'attendent désormais les électeurs de leur nouvel élu ? Valentin Cacheux leur a posé la question dans les rues de Détroit.

france24fr.title: VAGUE BLEUE : LE CAMP MAGA À L’ÉPREUVE ?
france24fr.description:
Les démocrates remportent une large victoire aux élections de mi-mandat. Un revers pour Donald Trump et le camp MAGA, déjà divisés sur la guerre en Iran. Cette vague bleue peut-elle infléchir la politique américaine au Moyen-Orient, en Ukraine et en Europe ?
 
Richard Werly, correspondant France-Europe pour le quotidien suisse Blick et auteur de Cette Amérique qui nous déteste, analyse les conséquences de ce scrutin.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Midterms en direct : la guerre en Iran "valait la peine" malgré la défaite électorale, juge Donald Trump
L'actu en dessin : le président Trump submergé par une vague démocrate lors des midterms
france24fr.description: Une vague démocrate a déferlé jusque dans des bastions républicains lors des élections de mi-mandat, alimentée par la colère suscitée par la flambée des prix de l'énergie et la longue guerre contre l'Iran. Un vote sanction qui constitue une humiliation personnelle pour le président américain Donald Trump, même s'il a dit ne pas se sentir visé, et qui hypothèque ses deux dernières années de mandat.

france24fr.title: Une "maison de torture" à Kiev ? Comment la photo d'un enfant a été instrumentalisée par la Russie
france24fr.description: Lundi, près de Kiev, des rumeurs de torture dans un centre de détention de déserteurs géré par la Garde nationale ukrainienne ont déclenché une manifestation violente. La diplomatie russe et des responsables d'extrême droite européens ont par la suite diffusé la photo d'un adolescent présenté comme une victime du centre. Ce dernier faisait en fait partie des manifestants.

france24fr.title: Midterms : Donald Trump face au verdict des urnes

spiegel.description: Nach 206 Jahren hat die Adler-Apotheke am Markt in Werne geschlossen. Hier erklärt Friederich Schneider, wie er mit dem Abschied klarkommt – und damit, der vielleicht letzte Apotheker seiner Familie zu sein.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Alexander Zverev wirft Becker vor, »relativ viel Blödsinn« zu erzählen
spiegel.description: In einem SPIEGEL-Interview versuchte Boris Becker, fehlende Sympathien in Deutschland für Alexander Zverev zu erklären. Der konterte nun scharf. Becker suche nach allem, um ihn runterzumachen.

observador.title: Desarmar bactérias com a ajuda da inteligência artificial
observador.description: Em 2022, Ricardo Monteiro procurava uma molécula capaz de desarmar uma bactéria perigosa para grávidas. Até agora já analisou mais de 200 milhões de compostos e chegou a 12 hipóteses promissoras.

observador.title: RDCongo tem a pior epidemia de cólera em décadas
observador.description: A época das chuvas e os conflitos armados dificultam o combate à pior epidemia de cólera em 25 anos na RDCongo, que já convive com um surto de Ébola devastador.

observador.title: Trump defende que eventual impeachment destruiria democratas
observador.description: Na primeira aparição pública após as eleições intercalares, Trump respondeu à ameaça de impeachment e garantiu que não tenciona demitir o secretário da Defesa, Pete Hegseth.

observador.title: "Presidente no comando". Governo reconhece vitória de Seguro
observador.description: Seguro queria Ventura, Carneiro e (sobretudo) Montenegro à mesma mesa. E conseguiu. Declaração do PM ao país com impressão digital do Presidente. "Está no comando", celebram os apoiantes de Seguro.

observador.title: FCP x Napoli. “Gabri Veiga é quem marca os tempos”
observador.description: Para Luís Pinto Coelho, Froholdt "está distante do que fez na época passada", Højlund, do Nápoles, "é um ponta de lança de topo" e, tirando uns minutos da primeira parte, o Porto mandou no jogo.

observador.title: Bob Dylan encontrou-se com o Papa no Vaticano
observador.description: O músico, de 85 anos, ofereceu a autobiografia "Crónicas – Vol.1" ao pontífice, que lhe deu um rosário. Leão XIV já tinha citado versos de Dylan num livro publicado este ano.

observador.title: Gabri, um deputado europeu para trazer união
observador.description: Depois de três derrotas em três jornadas, o FC Porto tirou a barriga de misérias e goleou o Nápoles para alcançar a primeira vitória na Champions. Gabri assistiu, marcou e voltou a ser o melhor (4-1).

observador.title: Ministra e MP 'alinham' no pagamento a advogados oficiosos
observador.description: Rita Alarcão Júdice assinou a portaria esta quarta-feira. O MP já defendeu a inconstitucionalidade da norma que obriga advogados a esperar pelo trânsito em julgado para ser pagos.

observador.title: Morreu Tinto Brass, realizador de "Calígula"
observador.description: Discípulo de Rossellini, o cineasta começou no cinema experimental mas ascendeu ao estrelato quando abraçou o erotismo. Foi homenageado este ano no Festival de Veneza.

observador.title: Suspeitos de facilitar tráfico de cocaína detidos
observador.description: Detenção ocorreu no decurso de uma investigação de cerca de dois meses no combate ao tráfico de droga. Estupefacientes seriam provenientes da América do Sul. Detidos estão em prisão preventiva.

observador.title: A1 parcialmente reaberta no sentido sul-norte após acidente
observador.description: A circulação esteve cortada desde as 18h24 após a ocorrência de um incêndio em duas viaturas. Pelas 19h25 mantinham-se 20 operacionais no local. Não há registo de feridos.

observador.title: Milhares de estudantes protestam em Copenhaga
observador.description: Estudantes contestam o corte feito ao apoio dado pelo Governo. A manifestação, segundo os organizadores, reuniu mais de 10.000 alunos e decorreu sem incidentes.

observador.title: Governo prevê 88 milhões para manter professores nas escolas
observador.description: As despesas com pessoal representam 94,7% do orçamento para a área da Educação. Dentro das medidas está uma parceria com estabelecimentos de ensino superior para dar formação a quem já exerce.

observador.title: Finlândia apoia deslocados com alimentos comprados à Ucrânia
observador.description: Arroz e óleo de soja comprados à Ucrânia chegaram esta quarta-feira a Pemba. Cabo Delgado enfrenta uma crise humanitária com 6.600 mortos e 1,3 milhões de deslocados desde 2017.

observador.title: Suspeito de pornografia de menores em prisão preventiva
observador.description: O homem de 35 anos tinha milhares de ficheiros com conteúdo de exploração sexual na sua posse. Depois da aplicação da medida, o arguido foi levado para o estabelecimento prisional de Elvas.

observador.title: 21h. Trump acredita que impugnação destruiria os Democratas
observador.description: Após a derrota nas intercalares, Trump afirmou estar confiante de que não vai haver destituição. Ainda, imigrantes que desobedecerem à polícia podem perder a residência portuguesa.

observador.title: Municípios promovem encontro nacional sobre habitação
observador.description: O evento, que ocorrerá em Fátima, pretende juntar responsáveis institucionais e representantes do setor. O ponto central será o aumento do parque habitacional público que ainda está na casa dos 2%.

observador.title: Provocador e 1.º muçulmano no Senado. Quem é Abdul El-Sayed?
observador.description: Rejeita assumir-se como socialista, mas é de esquerda. Abdul El-Sayed polarizou campanha, mas conquistou lugar no Senado no Michigan. Progressistas democratas tomam nota e centristas inquietam-se.

nyt.title: With Democrats’ Sweep, Congress Is Set to Reassert Power to Check Trump
nyt.description: President Trump usurped power from the legislative branch with Republican help for two years. Democrats are now positioned to try to claw back some of Congress’s prerogatives.

nyt.title: Five Things to Know About Hakeem Jeffries
nyt.description: The New York Democrat who is in line to be the first Black speaker was raised in Brooklyn, is a moderate who is cautious by nature and loves a hip-hop reference.

nyt.title: On the Democrats’ Agenda: Investigations of Trump and His Family
nyt.description: When a new Congress is sworn in, it will have the power to hold hearings and issue subpoenas, prompting one representative to advise White House officials and others to “lawyer up.”

nyt.title: Stocks Rise as Democrats Flip Control of Congress
nyt.description: Markets traded higher as investors foresaw gridlock in Washington, typically a bullish signal.

nyt.title: SpaceX and Tesla Stocks Tumble After Elon Musk-Backed Candidates Lose in Texas
nyt.description: The world’s richest person has antagonized Democrats, some of whom have signaled their intent to investigate him when they take control of Congress.

nyt.title: Israel’s President Could Play Key Role in Breaking Post-Election Deadlock
nyt.description: President Isaac Herzog has tried to avoid controversy and heal rifts in his largely ceremonial role. But his skills as a savvy mediator could be instrumental after an inconclusive election.

nyt.title: For ‘Dune: Part Three,’ Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya and Friends Weigh in on the Trilogy
nyt.description: As Denis Villeneuve’s blockbuster series concludes, the cast recalls dealing with desert shoots and wrestling with the story’s moral implications.

nyt.title: Could a Viral Video Save Her Mom’s Chinese Restaurant?
nyt.description: Millions viewed Lisa He’s post about her mother’s struggling business in Edinburgh. But internet fame created its own complications — and obscured bigger questions.

nyt.title: CVS to Split Off Drugstore Business, Ending Its Bigger-Is-Better Era
nyt.description: In a breakup planned for 2028, CVS Health intends to keep together its insurance and pharmacy benefits divisions and create a separate company for its pharmacies.

nyt.title: Appeals Court Allows Mamdani to Move Forward with Pied-à-Terre Tax
nyt.description: The court reversed a judge’s order that had said New York erred in its rollout of the tax, granting Mayor Zohran Mamdani a victory over a key piece of his agenda.

nyt.title: The Southwest Is Parched. Can the Recent Floodwaters Quench It?
nyt.description: A series of storms has added to reservoirs in the Colorado River basin, but the long-term water outlook remains bleak.

nyt.title: Trump Wanted Democrats to Win
nyt.description: The president loves combat and chaos. He’s about to get more of it.

nyt.title: These Midterms Show That Trump Blew It
nyt.description: There was nothing inevitable about this comeuppance.

nyt.title: Key Part of Jet in Deadly Florida Crash Found Far From Impact Site
nyt.description: The mechanism that controls the vertical angle of the plane was found in three pieces, including one nearly four miles away. All nine people aboard were killed.

republika.title: Como a valanga sul campo del Lens: 9-1 e 4° posto. Tripletta per Douvikas
republika.description: Incredibile prestazione degli uomini di Fabregas: solo il Bayern nel 2024 aveva segnato 9 reti in una gara di Champions

republika.description: McTominay nel primo tempo risponde a Bednarek, nella ripresa gli azzurri scompaiono dal campo e incassano il terzo ko in quattro giornate di Champions

republika.description: Perquisizioni della polizia nei confronti del dj Ludovico Franchitti: avrebbe contribuito a ricattare il giocatore sfruttando i suoi debiti di gioco. Cinque indagati

republika.description: Il cantante e premio Nobel per la letteratura, a Roma per un concerto, indossava una felpa nera con cappuccio. Era accompagnato da padre Spadaro che aveva portato dal Pontefice anche Patti Smith. Prevost aveva citato la canzone mai cantata sull’atomica

republika.title: Serena Grandi: “Tinto Brass mi ha regalato una carriera. Altre colleghe lo hanno rinnegato, io mai”
republika.description: L’attrice protagonista del film “Miranda” ricorda il regista morto oggi a 93 anni

republika.title: Tinto Brass e gli ultimi mesi da “prigioniero” a Isola Farnese: la frana e l’appello a Mattarella
republika.description: Il regista viveva da oltre cinquant’anni nel borgo alle porte di Roma. Il crollo dell'unica strada di accesso lo aveva costretto a fare i conti con le difficoltà negli spostamenti e nelle cure mediche. Fino alla lettera al presidente della Repubblica

republika.title: Francia, attacco ibrido a celle frigorifere con il sangue dei donatori. Anche l’Italia alza la guardia
republika.description: La ministra della Salute ha annunciato che non c’è stato “alcun impatto sanitario”. Luciana Teofili, direttrice del Centro nazionale sangue (Cns): “Dopo quello che è successo, è necessario anche qui tenere alta l’attenzione”

republika.title: Stati Uniti, tutti i primati storici delle midterm
republika.description: Dalla prima governatrice nativa eletta in New Mexico al primo latino alla guida della California: queste elezioni hanno spezzato la maggioranza repubblicana e abbattuto alcune barriere storiche

republika.title: Tinto Brass, intellettuale e “sporcaccione”: le due anime del regista fedele solo a se stesso
republika.description: Il regista è morto a 93 anni. Aveva esordito nel 1963 con un film girato a Venezia, “Chi lavora è perduto”, che era purissima Nouvelle Vague e sembrava portare in laguna le istanze stilistiche e politiche di Godard

republika.title: Tinto Brass, l’intervista per i 90 anni: “L’amore è la sola trasgressione che ci resta”
republika.description: Infanzia veneziana, esordi engagé, successo, politica, scandali. “Ho scoperto l’autoerotismo in spiaggia e ai giovani dico: sperimentate”

republika.title: Midterm, le conseguenze della sconfitta di Trump su Netanyahu
republika.description: Dall’incognita della ripresa del conflitto con l’Iran ai finanziamenti militari allo Stato ebraico fino all’attenzione sul senatore musulmano El-Sayed

republika.title: Leone XIV: “La guerra è un fallimento della politica, prendersi cura delle ferite dei popoli”
republika.description: All’udienza generale in piazza San Pietro il Papa torna agli insegnamenti sociali del Concilio: “Lo sviluppo economico deve essere al servizio dell’uomo, purtroppo ancora oggi non sempre è equo e rispettoso del creato”

republika.title: Caso Garlasco, cosa succede ora: il paradosso giuridico è un rompicapo anche per gli esperti
republika.description: Quattro gli scenari che si aprono: due condannati, nessuno, Sempio al posto di Stasi che ha già scontato gran parte della sua pena, oppure tutto confermato senza modifiche

republika.title: Radicali e moderati insieme si può, la lezione americana sul centrosinistra: uniti sui temi sociali
republika.description: La vittoria dei democratici alle midterm dimostra che le due anime possono convivere ma serve "una svolta in favore di chi ha meno”, dice Bonaccini. Ruotolo: da Mamdani a El-Sayed bisogna puntare su sanità, lavoro, lotta alle diseguaglianze

republika.title: Centrodestra freddo su midterm, i leghisti scaricano Trump: “Deve tornare a essere Maga”
republika.description: Il vicecapogruppo del Carroccio alla Camera Iezzi: “Far la guerra non paga”. Da via della Scrofa, quartier generale di FdI: “Ci aspettavamo un risultato negativo”

republika.title: L’onda dem su Trump ora fa tremare Big Tech: i colossi temono una stretta sui data center
republika.description: Con la vittoria alle midterm dei Democratici, il Presidente non ha più il sostegno del Congresso. Cosa si aspettano i mercati dal nuovo scenario

republika.title: Russia, è morto a 81 anni uno dei creatori del Novichok
republika.description: Vladimir Uglev è stato uno degli sviluppatori dell'agente nervino usato per avvelenare fra gli altri Navalny nel 2020 e Sergei e Yulia Skripal, nel 2018

npr.title: Abdul El-Sayed welcomes Trump's plan to cut Israel aid, calls for end to arms sales
npr.description: Michigan's first Muslim senator-elect, Abdul El-Sayed, discusses his historic victory, an unlikely agreement with Trump on Israel military aid and the political divisions that remain.

npr.title: The world is reacting to the Democrats' sweeping midterm elections victory
npr.description: From Kyiv to Moscow, and Tehran to Tel Aviv, all eyes were on the Democrats' big win as foreign powers weigh how a flipped Congress will affect international relations.

npr.title: Democrats seize full control of Congress. And, which candidates made history last night
npr.description: Democrats have won the House and the Senate, taking full control of Congress for the first time since 2023. And history was made in several states. Here's what happened last night.

npr.title: Japan faces diplomatic dilemma amid joint pressure from nuclear neighbors
npr.description: As the Ukraine war grinds on, ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo wants more support from Washington, but some Japanese are concerned they may not get it.

npr.title: For Ukraine's Kherson region, a short ceasefire meant a momentary return to normal life
npr.description: In Kherson city, usually seething with Russian drones, friends met at cafes, families were out together and shoppers stocked up. "The city seems alive," said one resident, "just like it used to be."

npr.title: Indian navy rescues 20 crew from Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia
npr.description: he operation involved a warship, a maritime surveillance aircraft and marine commandos. The hijacking followed a resurgence of Somali piracy across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean.

npr.title: Control of Congress is at stake today. And, judge to consider motion in Clancy case
npr.description: Election Day is here, and voters are heading to the polls in an election that may change control of Congress. And, a judge is considering whether to dismiss Lindsay Clancy's murder case.

npr.title: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing
npr.description: Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.

npr.title: Haley Stevens backs Mike Rogers. And, Gulf states brace for potential attack on Iran
npr.description: Democrats in Michigan are considering their options after Haley Stevens endorsed GOP candidate Mike Rogers for Senate. And the Gulf states are bracing for a possible U.S. attack on Iran after the midterms.

npr.title: Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
npr.description: The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.

elpais.title: El presidente de Adif presenta su dimisión a Cuerpo tras explicar el suceso de Urda
elpais.description: Luis Pedro Marco de la Peña ha acudido al encuentro con el nuevo titular de Transportes después de que haya sido aprobado por el consejo de Adif un marco de financiación de 20.000 millones hasta 2030 para obras y mantenimiento

elpais.title: Una crisis ferroviaria y aplacar a un sector constructor en contra, los desafíos de Cuerpo tras la ‘era Puente’
elpais.description: El vicepresidente asume el mando en Transportes con la urgencia de aplicar las reformas de seguridad en la alta velocidad y decidir sobre la cúpula de Adif, pero también con contratos de obra pública en desequilibrio por la crisis de Ormuz

elpais.title: España pide ayuda a Bruselas para llevar a cabo la investigación del accidente de Urda
elpais.description: La agencia ferroviaria europea dará apoyo técnico a los investigadores españoles

elpais.description: El vicepresidente, J. D. Vance, había previamente señalado el conflicto como la causa de la debacle republicana en las legislativas

elpais.description: La mitad de los distritos se ha movido más de 14 puntos hacia los demócratas, y 307 lo han hecho más de 10

elpais.title: ¿Cómo puede el nuevo Congreso de EE UU prohibir la guerra de Irán?
elpais.description: Josep Borrell, exalto representante de la Unión Europea para Asuntos Exteriores y Política de Seguridad, en el marco de WIP, explica lo cerca que están los demócratas de superar el veto de Donald Trump en temas de política exterior

elpais.title: ¿Y ahora qué? Demócratas y republicanos empiezan a diseñar sus estrategias tras el vuelco electoral
elpais.description: Trump coquetea con vetar las medidas de sus rivales; la nueva mayoría, con investigaciones a los miembros del gobierno

elpais.title: Las elecciones de la primera vez: los récords de mujeres, negros, gays, musulmanes, latinos e indígenas en las ‘midterms’
elpais.description: El-Sayed, primer senador musulmán. Pappas, primer senador gay. Hinojosa, primera gobernadora latina de Texas. Son algunos de los que rompen con sus victorias distintos techos de cristal

elpais.title: La victoria de la izquierda en las urnas: el efecto del verano socialista de Zohran Mamdani llega a las ‘midterms’
elpais.description: Al menos cinco de los candidatos Socialistas Democráticos, que pertenecen al sector más progresista del Partido Demócrata, irán a la Cámara de Representantes

elpais.title: Acorralado en la Casa Blanca, Trump puede ser más peligroso para el mundo
elpais.description: La autonomía que el presidente de Estados Unidos tiene para marcar la política exterior puede convertirse su refugio para seguir sembrando el caos

elpais.description: Los ayuntamientos terminan este miércoles los sorteos para elegir a los presidentes, vocales y suplentes. Los seleccionados recibirán una notificación

elpais.description: Tras un partido gris, el equipo de Mourinho se lleva su cuarta victoria en el arreón final del tiempo añadido con un golazo de Fede Valverde

elpais.description: El nuevo libro de la autora chilena, continuación de ‘La casa de los espíritus’ 44 años después, tiene menos fantasmas y más fascismo del mundo terrenal

elpais.description: La escritora catalana reflexiona que lo que caracteriza a su creación es “lo inquietante”

phys-org.title: Feejee Mermaid on display in Colorado may shock and intrigue—but no longer considered a 'missing link'
phys-org.description: Mermaids have inhabited world folklore and mythology for centuries. Ancient Babylonians worshiped Oannes, a human-fish hybrid; sirens populated Greek mythology; and fairy tales such as "The Little Mermaid" have made this figure a pop culture icon.

phys-org.title: Cosmic hydrogen measurement marks breakthrough in mapping the universe
phys-org.description: An international research project is bringing scientists closer to mapping the universe. The MeerKLASS Collaboration has reported its first measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen, advancing a technique that could transform how cosmologists chart the universe.

phys-org.title: Corporate green reports: Do independent checks really help companies deliver measurable action?
phys-org.description: The European Union's Omnibus reform has exempted most of the companies it once covered from mandatory sustainability reporting under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). It has also dropped plans for tougher "reasonable" assurance checks on green claims, which come closer to a full audit.

phys-org.title: Traditional Korean paper becomes breathable patch for future wearable health care
phys-org.description: Wearable health-monitoring devices are becoming increasingly important for personalized health care, but conventional patches often rely on substrates that restrict airflow, trap sweat and cause skin discomfort during prolonged use. These limitations can also interfere with the reliable collection and analysis of sweat, highlighting the need for breathable materials that support both comfortable wear and accurate sensing.

phys-org.title: NOAA, NASA release measurements of 2026 ozone hole
phys-org.description: Atypical weather conditions caused the Antarctic ozone hole to grow to an unusually large size in 2026, NOAA and NASA scientists reported today, though they said the protective ozone layer is still on track to recover by later this century.

phys-org.title: Molecular choreography: How the p97 protein regulates cellular quality control
phys-org.description: The p97 protein plays a central role in cellular quality control by preparing defective or no-longer-needed proteins for degradation and recycling. Researchers at the University of Münster, in collaboration with the University of Duisburg-Essen, have investigated how p97 and its auxiliary proteins interact in this process. The study has now been published in the journal Nature Communications.

phys-org.title: Bio-based smart coating combines fire protection, early warning and upcyclability
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a multifunctional fire-protective coating that not only shields materials from extreme heat but also provides an early warning of fire and can be recycled into new flame-retardant materials at the end of its life. The work, published in Polymer Degradation and Stability, demonstrates a strategy for combining fire safety, sustainability and circularity within a single material system.

phys-org.title: New research uncovers chiral topological phases in metals without structural order
phys-org.description: Fermions are among the most important particles in physics and include both everyday electrons and more exotic variants. Chiral fermions, like gloves, come in left- and right-handed versions and were proposed over a century ago. While high-energy neutrinos—the leading candidates for massless chiral fermions—proved to have mass, nearly (semi-) metallic solid-state crystals were discovered 15 years ago to host electronic versions of massless chiral fermions.

phys-org.title: Why a company donating $20,000 a month counts for more than $240,000 once a year in the eyes of customers
phys-org.description: People tend to think more highly of companies that give to charity on a monthly or weekly basis rather than donating an annual lump sum worth the same amount.

phys-org.title: A cosmic 'leaf blower': Light-propelled winds help explain early universe's bright galaxies

Based on what they knew about the early universe, such galaxies should have been far less common in the few hundred million years following the Big Bang.

It disrupts biological processes at all levels—from genes to entire ecosystems—and contributes significantly to global biodiversity loss. phys-org.description: The genital structures of male hawkmoths are lifesavers. By rubbing specialized scales on their genitals against parts of their abdomen, the nocturnal insects emit ultrasonic sounds that can potentially scramble the acoustic signals that bats use to hunt.

phys-org.title: Northern permafrost greening masks declining plant resilience, study finds
phys-org.description: An international study jointly led by researchers from the Department of Geography and the Institute for Climate and Carbon Neutrality at the Faculty of Social Sciences, The University of Hong Kong (HKU), has revealed that vegetation resilience across Northern Hemisphere permafrost regions underwent a widespread reversal around 2008, declining broadly despite continued greening.

phys-org.title: Gold mining introduces an overlooked threat to wild caimans
phys-org.description: Mercury pollution from artisanal gold mining in tropical regions is finding its way into wildlife. A team from the University of Vienna and the Veterinary University of Vienna shows that mercury exposure impairs the glucocorticoid response that helps animals cope with acute stress. This weakened stress response could reduce the caimans' chances of survival and reproduction. phys-org.title: New CO₂ sensor combines high sensitivity with a wider measurement range
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science (HFIPS) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) have developed a carbon dioxide (CO₂) sensor that combines high sensitivity with a wider measurement range.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?

But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.

proj-syn.title: The Rise and Fall of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Privacy is not a natural phenomenon, but rather a historical achievement. It emerged after the Reformation and the wars of religion that followed, reached a high point during the Victorian era, and has now been eroding for decades, long before the advent of the digital economy, social media, and AI.

proj-syn.title: Good Institutions Require Good People
proj-syn.description: Well-designed laws, courts, catechisms, extrinsic motives, social approval, and even a few good and decent people are of no avail if too many people do not behave like self-respecting and other-respecting adults. Childish pride and envy, grabbing more of the sweets, Donald Trump-style, do not make for a good society.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchic World Order
proj-syn.description: Today, some 64 heads of state or government are oligarchs, leading countries that together account for some 60% of global GDP. The question is thus no longer whether oligarchs will rule the world, but rather what kind of world they are building.

proj-syn.title: Poland’s Constitutional Civil War
proj-syn.description: Polish right-wing populists recently stormed the country's Constitutional Tribunal, winning applause from the Kremlin and far-right fellow-travelers across Europe. As in other countries, the constitutional tribunal is the institution that distinguishes a proper democracy from a dictatorship making it a target for authoritarians.

proj-syn.title: The Tech Brotherhood Wants Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: After centuries of nation-states, a new form of sovereignty is asserting itself. The small fraternity that controls the major digital platforms has already proven capable of even more intrusive and insidious forms of control than most states can muster.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Tariff Fiasco Could Save Free Trade
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have raised prices and hurt businesses without reducing the trade deficit or creating manufacturing jobs. But global trade has held up better than expected, and growing public opposition to tariffs could pave the way for a retreat from protectionism.

proj-syn.title: If AI Thinks for Us, Democracy Will Suffer
proj-syn.description: Whereas the internet buried us in information, AI enables us to outsource analysis altogether. But when it comes to grappling with humanity’s most important questions, we must resist the temptation and recognize that we all have a duty—to each other and to ourselves—to keep “showing up.”

proj-syn.title: A Tory Mentor for the MAGA GOP
proj-syn.description: Kemi Badenoch’s keynote address at the British Conservative Party conference last month outlined her plan for a pro-growth future that respects fiscal discipline and human dignity. As American conservatives look beyond Donald Trump and to the 2028 primary campaign, they should embrace a similar agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Politics of Poland’s Judicial Crisis
proj-syn.description: The removal of Bogdan Święczkowski as president of the Constitutional Tribunal has triggered a physical confrontation at the court and a political standoff between Donald Tusk’s government and the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party. But Święczkowski was not so much removed as barred, because he held the position illegally.

proj-syn.title: Mapping AI Resistance
proj-syn.description: Since a society that is reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains, it is worth understanding why the AI revolution is being welcomed in some places and resisted in others. The explanation is not as simple as headline poll data and much media coverage suggest.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Perilous Ebola Complacency
proj-syn.description: The exponential trajectory of the latest Ebola outbreak is an urgent reminder that infectious diseases do not wait for ideal geopolitical alignments or balanced budgets. Global leaders must fund the Africa-led regional response today, or risk paying an immeasurably higher price in human lives and economic devastation tomorrow.
